package_info.package_name: Popup Builder WordPress plugin (malicious Custom JS injection)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all vulnerable versions with stored XSS flaw)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers exploit a stored XSS vulnerability in the Popup Builder plugin to inject malicious JavaScript into the Custom JS or CSS sections. This allows arbitrary code execution in site visitors' browsers, leading to unauthorized redirections, credential/session theft, and malware delivery.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits an infected site page
execution_context.file_location: Popup Builder plugin's Custom JS section (stored in WordPress database, rendered in page HTML)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user visits an infected page, the code executes in the browser, accesses document.cookie, appends the cookie value to a malicious URL, and redirects the browser to the attacker's domain, resulting in credential/session exfiltration and potential further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code directly accesses sensitive cookie data and exfiltrates it by redirecting the user's browser to an attacker-controlled domain, which is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Custom JS in WordPress plugins is intended to enhance site functionality or appearance, not to access sensitive data or perform unauthorized redirections to external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate redirection scripts may be used for navigation or login flows, but never to transmit cookies or sensitive data to untrusted, external domains.
key_indicators: Direct use of document.cookie in client-side code
Hardcoded external domain in window.location assignment
Use of <script> tag in plugin's Custom JS section

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits an infected site page
execution_context.file_location: Popup Builder plugin's Custom JS section (stored in WordPress database, rendered in page HTML)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user visits an infected page, the code loads and executes a remote JavaScript payload from an attacker-controlled server, enabling arbitrary code execution in the victim's browser, which can result in further malware injection, credential theft, or drive-by downloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and executing remote scripts from untrusted, non-whitelisted domains is a common technique for delivering malware and taking control of user sessions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Custom JS should not load code from external, untrusted sources, especially without user consent or validation. Loading scripts from unknown domains exposes users to arbitrary code execution risks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate sites may load scripts from trusted CDNs (e.g., Google, Cloudflare), but not from unknown or suspicious domains without integrity checks.
key_indicators: External script source from non-whitelisted, attacker-controlled domain
No integrity or authenticity checks on loaded script
Potential for arbitrary code execution in browser context
Use of <script src=...> in plugin configuration

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits a stored XSS vulnerability in the Popup Builder plugin to inject malicious JavaScript into the Custom JS section.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is stored in the WordPress database and rendered on site pages.

attack_chain.action: When a user visits an infected page, the malicious JavaScript executes in their browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected to an attacker-controlled domain and/or additional malware is loaded in the browser.

attack_chain.action: The malicious domain receives exfiltrated data (such as cookies) or delivers further payloads to the victim's browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential or session theft, further compromise of the user's account, or malware infection.

behavioral_signatures: Custom JS or CSS in WordPress plugins containing <script> tags with direct access to document.cookie
Custom JS loading external scripts from non-whitelisted or suspicious domains
Unexpected client-side redirections to external domains not associated with the legitimate site
file_indicators: Popup Builder plugin's Custom JS or CSS fields containing suspicious JavaScript code
Presence of <script>window.location=... or <script src=... in plugin configuration fields
Custom JS fields referencing document.cookie or external domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests from site visitors' browsers to unknown or suspicious domains (e.g., malicious-domain.com)
Redirections to domains not associated with the legitimate site
Loading of remote JavaScript payloads from non-whitelisted domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the Custom JS and CSS fields of the Popup Builder plugin for suspicious <script> tags, especially those accessing document.cookie or loading external scripts from untrusted domains. Analyze web traffic for unexpected redirections or requests to non-whitelisted domains. Deploy web application firewalls (WAF) to block or alert on script injections and outbound connections to known malicious domains. Regularly audit plugin configurations for unauthorized changes.
